newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-TIMBERWOLVES FINALLY CRACK .500 MARK.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-TIMBERWOLVES FINALLY CRACK .500 MARK.

text.p: The Minnesota Timberwolves have finally won more games than they lost.
For the first time in franchise history the Timberwolves are over the .500 mark later than the first month of the NBA season after a 108-89 rout of the San Antonio Spurs Wednesday.
Tom Gugliotta scored 29 points to lead Minnesota to a pair of milestones as the 28-27 Timberwolves also picked up a club-record 10th road win.
"This is a big one for us and it gives us the opportunity to build on it," Minnesota coach Flip Saunders said.

Kevin Garnett scored 17 points and Dean Garrett added 16 for the Timberwolves, who were 2-1 and 4-3 in November and and 1-0 in 1990 in their only previous forays beyond .500 since joining the league in 1989.
Dominique Wilkins scored 20 points and Will Perdue added 19 and 17 rebounds for San Antonio, which fell to 13-42 and is assured of its first losing season since 1989.
"They are playing hard and they are hungry to get a taste of success," Spurs guard Vinny Del Negro said of Minnesota.
At Detroit, Lindsey Hunter and Terry Mills scored 21 points apiece as the Pistons crushed the Golden State Warriors by 33 points, 117-84.
Joe Dumars added 19 points and Grant Hill had 13 and 10 assists for Detroit, winner of seven of its last eight games.
Latrell Sprewell netted 19 points and Chris Mullin had 15 for Golden State, which fell to 0-4 on a six-game road swing.
Golden State jumped out to a 7-1 lead before Detroit took over with a 16-2 run, sparked by eight points by Hill.
In Orlando, Dennis Scott and Rony Seikaly scored 26 points apiece as the Magic remained unbeaten under interim coach Richie Adubato with a 98-86 victory over the Miami Heat.
Penny Hardaway added 18 points and seven assists for the Magic, who led by as many as 20 points.
In their final five games under Brian Hill the Magic went 0-5, allowing an average of 107.6 points per game. They are 5-0 under Adubato and allowing 86 points per game.
Jamal Mashburn scored 21 points the Heat, who are without injured star centre Alonzo Mourning.

At Indiana, Reggie Miller scored seven of his 22 points in a game-ending 20-6 run that lifted the Pacers to a 92-78 victory over the Seattle SuperSonics, who had their seven-game winning streak snapped.
Rik Smits and Duane Ferrell added 14 each for Indiana.
Shawn Kemp had 19 points and 11 rebounds and Gary Payton scored 18 points for the Sonics, who went scoreless for nearly seven minutes in the fourth quarter.
In Boston, Mitch Richmond scored 38 points to lead the Sacramento Kings to their first road win over the Celtics in more than 18 years, 111-105.
Billy Owens added 20 points and Olden Polynice just missed a triple-double with 16 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists for the Kings, who had lost their previous 17 games in Boston.
Rick Fox had 25 points and Antoine Walker chipped in 24 for the Celtics, losers of 11 in a row.
In Milwaukee, Steve Smith scored eight of his 21 points in the third quarter, when the Atlanta Hawks limited the Bucks to a franchise-low eight points en route to a 79-72 victory.
Mookie Blaylock had 18 points and Dikembe Mutombo added 14 and 11 rebounds for the Hawks
Glenn Robinson scored 22 points to lead Milwaukee, which managed just 25 points in the second half.
In Phoenix, Kevin Johnson scored 36 points to lead the Suns to a 111-104 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers.
Jason Kidd added 19 points, 13 assists, seven rebounds and six steals for the Suns, who blew an eight-point lead in the fourth quarter but recovered for the victory.
Johnson and Kidd ganged up on 76ers point guard Allen Iverson, holding him to just eight points on 3-of-15 shooting.
Jerry Stackhouse scored 28 points to pace the Sixers.
In Vancouver, Loy Vaught scored nine of his 22 points in the fourth quarter and added 13 rebounds as the Los Angeles Clippers beat the Grizzlies 83-80.
Malik Sealy sank a pair of free throws with 11 seconds remaining to give the Clippers their 83-80 edge.
Vancouver had a chance to tie, but Anthony Peeler's three-point attempt which fell short at the buzzer.
Lamond Murray added 13 points and 11 rebounds for Los Angeles. Shareef Abdur-Rahim had 28 points and 13 rebounds to pace Vancouver.
In Portland, Patrick Ewing scored five of his 27 points in overtime and the New York Knicks took advantage of a late turnover to edge the Trail Blazers 96-95.
Isaiah Rider made a reverse layin as the Blazers closed within 96-95 with 32 seconds to go.

But after Ewing missed a turnaround jumper with 13 seconds left, Portland blew a golden opportunity as Kenny Anderson penetrated the lane and passed to Gary Trent near the free-throw line. But Trent was stripped of the ball and the Knicks ran out the clock.
